text:
Captain

 Command a fleet of AI agents — on every deck, every desk, every wrist

 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 Most AI tools give you one agent in a chat box. Captain Flight Deck is a multi-agent command center: spawn specialist teams, run seven orchestration modes , ship software with Code (plan → build → independent review), and compose deterministic Flows . Self-hosted, MIT licensed, and it works with every major LLM provider, or 100% local with Ollama. Since 0.8.2 your Flight Decks work together : a planner on your VPS asks a researcher on the Raspberry Pi at home, and you watch the request cross a live map. Your team works from a kiosk ; you can just talk to a watch . Since 0.8.4 you can teach an agent your work and test it , and see every task on one Taskboard . Since 0.8.5 your agents run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Crush and Pi as their crew , and you can say what you need and get a whole team , with its schedules and its software. Since 0.8.6 everything they do on their own is on one Line , Captain Swarm makes them measurably better at your real work, and Captain for your desktop is a 75 MB download that updates itself. Since 0.8.8 they see what you see: Captain for Chrome sends the page you're on, and Captain for Mac sends what's on your screen from any app. Since 0.9.1 your private data stays yours: anonymization turns names, companies and numbers into tokens before a model sees them and puts them back when the answer comes home, and data rooms let Claude read a whole deal's files without learning who is in them. Since 0.9.2 they finish what they start: First Mate runs standing jobs on charters you approve, checked on every run, and your agents search and read the web in your own Chrome , signed in as you on LinkedIn and X. Since 0.9.3 you set how far they push: Drive runs from the first complete answer to an agent that checks itself and adds the obvious next step, and web playbooks give them 439 known ways through a website.

 New in 0.9.3 — Headway: Drive sets how far an agent pushes, from the first complete answer to one that checks itself and adds the obvious next step; 439 web playbooks with a store in Captain and in Captain for Chrome; Excel files as tables with a filter on every column; questions from MCP servers as cards; and a security fix every deck needs . Release notes · 0.9.2 — Landfall: First Mate runs standing jobs for you on charters you approve, within a weekly token budget; runs that keep going, save as they go, resume and check themselves until the goal is met; long lists finished by a list funnel that asks a model once per item; web searches and signed-in page reads in your own Chrome , for LinkedIn, X and every site that turns a server away; recordings an agent does again for you. Release notes · 0.9.1 — Strongroom: anonymization with an encrypted vault per case and a privacy gate for your agents; data rooms that give Claude a deal's files without the names; Vatra, Basna and Council in the kiosk; a new kiosk home. Release notes · 0.9.0 — Shipyard: tools of your own, built by Crew and run by Flight Deck in a sandbox; agents in one .captain file; agents that hand each other work, answer email meant for them and learn from corrections you approve. Release notes · Earlier: 0.8.11 — Hold · 0.8.10 — Provisions · 0.8.9 · 0.8.8 — Spyglass · 0.8.7 · 0.8.6 — Ship's Log 

 Drive: you set how far an agent pushes  ·  439 web playbooks  ·  First Mate: standing jobs that finish  ·  web search and signed-in reading in your own Chrome  ·  Flight Decks that work together  ·  Captain for Chrome and for Mac  ·  custom tools Crew builds for your agents  ·  anonymization and data rooms for Claude  ·  7 orchestration modes  ·  85 built-in tools per agent  ·  6 shared memory layers  ·  132 ready-made archetypes  ·  a full coding pipeline  ·  Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Crush and Pi as your crew  ·  a team-safe deck and kiosk  ·  voice devices from M5Stack and Waveshare  ·  living beings you raise  ·  small models that do real work 

 Why Captain

- 🛸 A fleet, not a chatbot. Spawn specialists from 132 ready-made archetypes (32 generalists and 100 specialists, for your industry or your own life) plus the ones your admin generates for your company, describe a goal and let Agent Forge design the whole team, or say what you need in your own words and Forge agents plans a standing team with its schedules and its software.
- 🏁 Work that gets finished. First Mate runs standing jobs on charters you approve: on a schedule or on new mail, within a weekly token budget, checked against the goals you set on every run, and nothing goes out until you've seen it. The runs underneath keep going while they make progress, resume where they stopped and know exactly what's still missing.
- 🎓 Agents you can train. Give an agent your documents and it keeps them whole at no token cost, reads what you budget for, and learns rules and facts you review. Then exam it, and see exactly where it went wrong It drafts lessons from your corrections for you to approve, works toward the goals you set on its Course , and fits in one file to back up, move to another deck or hand to a client.
- 🧩 The right shape for every problem. Seven orchestration modes, from blind ensembles merged by learned reliability to a collaborative blackboard, moderated councils, and a finisher that stops only when an independent judge says the work is done.
- 🛰️ Decks that work together. Flight Decks on a VPS, a laptop and a Raspberry Pi behind home NAT lend each other their agents over BotPort , and you watch every request cross a live map.
- 💻 An engineering department. Plan → your approval → build → three independent reviewers → fix, every phase a git commit in your own repo. Or hand
